hook: A boy, a wallet with 300 euros and a reward he turns down: read a true-to-life story for its facts and its reason.
intro: A true-to-life anecdote of about 190 words: a boy finds a wallet with three hundred euros and takes it to the police; the owner offers him fifty euros and he refuses — with a reason. It is told in the Präteritum (fand, lag, brachte, kam, lobte, bot … an, nahm) with one Konjunktiv II of the past — Viele Kinder hätten das Geld vielleicht behalten (many children might have kept the money) — the form you practised earlier in this module in the irreale-Wünsche quiz. Local newspapers love stories like this. The six questions want the facts (where, what, why late, how the teacher reacted, what the money was for) and the one reason (warum nahm er das Geld nicht?). Read for the sequence first, then for the numbers (dreihundert, fünfzig), then for the sentences with deshalb and als.
tips[0].title: Numbers are answers
tips[0].text: dreihundert Euro in the wallet; fünfzig Euro offered; zwölf years old. Underline every number on the first read — each one is a question or a distractor.
tips[0].check.why: zwanzig is the price, zwölf is what was paid: every number is either the answer or a distractor.
tips[1].title: hätten … behalten = what did not happen
tips[1].text: Viele Kinder hätten das Geld behalten is the Konjunktiv II of the past: hätte + participle. It describes what other children might have done — not what Tim did. His real action is in the Präteritum: brachte.
tips[1].check.why: hätten … behalten is what others might have done but didn't; Lisa's real action is in the Präteritum: gab zurück.
tips[2].title: zuerst …, doch als … = a change
tips[2].text: zuerst gives the first reaction, doch als … the change. Questions about feelings ask for the final state, not the first one.
tips[2].check.why: zuerst gives the first reaction; doch als … brings the change, and the final feeling is begeistert.
tips[2].visual.marks[0].label: first
tips[2].visual.marks[1].label: the turn
remember[0]: Numbers first, then the reasons after deshalb and in the quotation.
remember[1]: hätte + participle = what would have happened but did not.
exam: Short true-to-life stories like this are a standard reading text in the B1 exam — and in any local paper.
tips[1].check.q: „Andere hätten die Tasche behalten, aber Lisa gab sie zurück.“ What did Lisa do?
